learn: A computer is a machine that follows instructions to help people.
Computers can be big, like a desktop, or small, like a tablet or a phone.
Many things have tiny computers inside: cars, microwaves, even some toys.
check: Can a microwave have a tiny computer inside?
lessons.try: Find three things at home that have a computer inside.

learn: The screen shows pictures and words. The keyboard has letter keys.
The mouse moves the arrow on the screen. Speakers make sound.
A tablet's screen is also a touchscreen. You tap it with your finger.
check: On a touchscreen you use your...
lessons.try: Point to the screen, keyboard and mouse on a computer and name them.

learn: Computers cannot think by themselves. People write instructions for them.
The instructions are called programs or code.
People who write code are called programmers. You can be one too!
check: Instructions for a computer are called...
lessons.try: Give a grown-up three instructions to follow, like a computer would.

learn: Our school has many computers: in the office, the library and the classroom.
The library computer helps find books.
The office computer keeps track of who is at school.
check: The office computer knows who is...
lessons.try: Walk around the school and count the computers you see.

learn: Long ago, computers were as big as a room.
Now a computer can fit in your pocket.
Computers keep getting smaller and faster.
check: Long ago computers were as big as a...
Today a computer can fit in your...
lessons.try: Draw a giant old computer and a tiny new one.

learn: Doctors use computers to look inside bodies.
Farmers use computers to help water plants.
Families use computers to talk to faraway people.
check: Computers help families talk to people who are...
lessons.try: Ask a grown-up how they use a computer at work.

learn: Press the power button to turn a computer on.
Wait for it to start before you touch things.
Ask a grown-up how to turn it off the right way.
check: To turn a computer on, press the...
To turn it off, we ask a...
lessons.try: Find the power button on a school computer.

learn: Keep food and drinks away from computers.
Use clean, dry hands.
Carry tablets with two hands.
lessons.try: Make a "computer care" poster.

learn: A computer follows instructions.
Computers are big and small and help many people.
We take care of computers.
lessons.try: Tell a friend three things a computer can do.

learn: To click, press the mouse button once and let go.
On a touchscreen, tapping is like clicking.
Hold the mouse gently, with your pointer finger on the left button.
check: To click you press the button...
lessons.try: Practice clicking on five pictures in a drawing program.

learn: To drag, press and hold, move, then let go. This is called drag and drop.
On a tablet, you drag with your finger.
Dragging is how we move pictures, puzzle pieces and files.
check: What do you do at the end of a drag?
lessons.try: Play a drag and drop puzzle game.

learn: Keep food and drinks away from computers.
Use clean, dry hands and be gentle with screens and keys.
Carry tablets with two hands.
check: Should you eat over a keyboard?
lessons.try: Make a class rules poster for caring for devices.

learn: Move the mouse and the arrow moves on the screen.
The arrow is called the pointer.
Move slowly to point at the right thing.
check: The arrow on the screen is the...
When the mouse moves, the pointer...
lessons.try: Point at five pictures without clicking.

learn: A double-click is two quick clicks.
It opens things on the computer.
Keep the mouse still when you double-click.
lessons.try: Double-click a picture to open it.

learn: Swipe: slide your finger across the screen.
Pinch: two fingers together to make things small.
Spread: two fingers apart to make things big.
check: Sliding your finger across the screen is a...
To make a picture bigger, spread two...
lessons.try: Zoom in and out on a picture with two fingers.

learn: Scrolling moves the page up and down.
Use the mouse wheel or swipe with a finger.
Scroll to see more of a page.
lessons.try: Scroll to find the picture at the bottom of a page.

learn: Hold the button down to draw a line.
Let go to stop drawing.
Practice makes smooth lines.
lessons.try: Draw a house with the mouse.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Mouse and Touch
learn: Point, click, double-click, drag.
Tap, swipe, pinch.
Gentle hands work best.
lessons.try: Finish a mouse and touch skills game.

learn: A sequence is steps in order. First, next, then, last.
Brushing teeth has steps: put on toothpaste, brush, rinse.
If the steps are out of order, things go wrong!
check: What comes first when brushing teeth?
If steps are out of order...
lessons.try: Put pictures of making a sandwich in order.

learn: A robot only does exactly what you say.
If you say walk forward two steps, it walks forward two steps.
You must give clear, exact steps.
lessons.try: Be a robot! A partner says forward, turn, stop, and you follow exactly.

learn: Arrows can show steps: up, down, left, right.
A path of arrows can lead a character to a goal, like a bunny to a carrot.
Count the squares carefully.
check: What should you do with squares?
lessons.try: Draw a grid and write arrows to get a bunny to a carrot.

learn: Socks go on before shoes.
The order of steps matters.
A wrong order gives a silly result.
lessons.try: Put picture cards of getting dressed in order.

learn: Get bread, add filling, put bread on top.
Each step is clear and small.
Instructions like this are an algorithm.
check: A list of steps is an...
The last step of a sandwich is bread on...
lessons.try: Tell a grown-up the steps to make a sandwich.

learn: First tells where to start.
Next tells the middle.
Last tells the end.
check: The word for the start is...
The word for the end is...
The middle step uses the word...
lessons.try: Retell your morning with first, next, last.

learn: Say "Take two steps forward," not "Go over there."
Clear words help others follow.
Computers need very clear directions.
lessons.try: Guide a friend to a chair with clear directions.

learn: Left and right help a robot turn.
Your left hand makes an L.
Turning changes the way you face.
check: A robot needs left and right to...
lessons.try: Play a left and right turning game.

learn: Steps go in order.
Clear steps make an algorithm.
First, next, last.
lessons.try: Write picture steps for brushing teeth.

learn: A pattern repeats: red, blue, red, blue, red, blue.
We can guess what comes next in a pattern.
Computers are very good at repeating patterns.
check: Red, blue, red, blue... what comes next?
lessons.try: Make a pattern with blocks and ask someone to guess the next one.

learn: Clap, stomp, clap, stomp is a pattern you can hear.
Jump, jump, spin is a pattern you can move.
We call the part that repeats the core.
check: Clap, stomp, clap, stomp... next is?
The part that repeats is the...
lessons.try: Make up a clap and stomp pattern and teach it to someone.

learn: Patterns are everywhere: stripes on a shirt, tiles on a floor, days of the week.
Finding patterns helps us solve problems faster.
Look closely to find what repeats.
check: Days of the week are a...
lessons.try: Go on a pattern hunt and find three patterns at home.

learn: Circle, square, circle, square.
The part that repeats is the core.
Find what comes next.
check: Circle, square, circle... what comes next?
The part that repeats is the...
lessons.try: Build a shape pattern with blocks.

learn: 1 block, 2 blocks, 3 blocks.
Each time it grows by one.
Growing patterns get bigger.
check: Each step of the staircase grows by...
lessons.try: Build a block staircase.

learn: Stripes on a zebra.
Petals on a flower.
Day and night repeat.
lessons.try: Find three patterns outside.

learn: Computers love patterns.
A pattern can be made with steps that repeat.
Spotting patterns makes code shorter.
lessons.try: Find the repeating steps in a dance.

learn: Choose two or three things.
Repeat them in the same order.
Ask a friend to guess what comes next.
check: To make a pattern, ___ things in order.
A friend can guess what comes...
lessons.try: Make a sticker pattern for a friend to finish.

learn: Repeating patterns.
Growing patterns.
Patterns in code.
lessons.try: Pattern hunt in the classroom.

learn: Sorting means putting things in groups that are alike.
We can sort by color, size or shape.
Computers sort things all the time, like photos or songs.
lessons.try: Sort a bag of buttons or crayons by color.

learn: A sorting rule tells where things go. Rule: animals that fly, animals that do not.
Everything must follow the rule.
Different rules make different groups.
check: A bird goes in the group...
lessons.try: Sort animal pictures by a rule you choose. Can someone guess your rule?

learn: We can put things in order from biggest to smallest.
Or from shortest to tallest.
Putting in order is another kind of sorting.
check: Biggest to smallest is a kind of...
Which goes first, smallest to biggest?
Shortest to tallest puts things in...
lessons.try: Line up five toys from smallest to biggest.

learn: Put circles with circles.
Put squares with squares.
A group shares something the same.
lessons.try: Sort a pile of shapes.

learn: Big things in one group.
Small things in another.
Some things are in the middle.
check: A big ball and a little ball: which goes in the big group?
Sorting by size uses big and...
Size groups can have a ___ group.
lessons.try: Sort toys into big, middle and small.

learn: Ask a question: does it have wheels?
Yes things go in one pile, no in another.
Computers sort with yes and no.
check: A bird for "Can it fly?" goes in...
A car for "Can it fly?" goes in...
lessons.try: Sort pictures by "Can it fly?"

learn: Count how many are in each group.
Which group has more?
Which has fewer?
check: 5 red and 3 blue: which has more?
2 cats and 4 dogs: which has fewer?
lessons.try: Count red and blue cubes.

learn: A chart shows groups with pictures.
Each picture stands for one thing.
Charts help us see more and fewer.
check: In a picture chart, each picture stands for...
lessons.try: Make a picture chart of favourite fruits.

learn: Sort by shape, size, colour.
Yes and no groups.
Count and chart.
check: Yes or no is a way to...
lessons.try: Sort the class library by type of book.

learn: A loop means doing something again and again.
Instead of saying jump, jump, jump, we can say jump 3 times.
Loops make instructions shorter.
lessons.try: Do a dance: clap 4 times, spin 2 times.

learn: Many songs repeat a chorus. That is like a loop.
Row, row, row your boat repeats row three times.
Spot the repeat and you have found a loop.
check: The chorus that repeats is like a...
In row, row, row your boat, how many times is row said at the start?
Spotting a repeat means you found a...
lessons.try: Sing a song and clap each time the chorus repeats.

learn: Forward, forward, forward can be forward 3 times.
A loop can make a robot walk around a square: forward, turn, four times.
Count how many times something repeats.
check: Forward 3 times is the same as...
How many times do you repeat to make a square?
lessons.try: Walk a square on the floor using forward and turn, four times.

learn: Some dances repeat steps.
Step, step, clap. Again and again.
A loop says how many times.
check: A dance that repeats has a...
Loops save us from saying steps...
lessons.try: Make up a dance that loops three times.

learn: We brush our teeth every morning.
The sun rises every day.
Things that repeat are like loops.
check: Something done every day is like a...
lessons.try: List three things you do every day.

learn: "Jump 5 times" is a loop of 5.
Count each time you go round.
Stop when you reach the number.
check: When do you stop the loop?
lessons.try: Do a loop of 5 jumps and count out loud.

Draw one petal, turn, again.
Loops make neat pictures.

"Repeat 4: hop" is short.

learn: Loops repeat steps.
Count how many times.
Loops make code short.
check: Loops are found in songs and...

learn: A bug is a mistake in the instructions.
When there is a bug, the program does something we did not want.
Everyone makes bugs. Programmers find and fix them.
check: When we find a bug, we...
lessons.try: Give a grown-up instructions with one mistake. Can they find the bug?

learn: To find a bug, check each step one at a time.
Ask: what did I want, and what happened?
The step where things went wrong is where the bug is.
check: What did I want and what happened?
lessons.try: Follow arrows on a path with one wrong arrow and find it.

learn: Fixing bugs takes patience. It is okay to try many times.
Saying not yet instead of I can't helps us keep going.
Each try teaches us something.
check: When a bug is hard to find, you should...
lessons.try: Build a block tower, and if it falls, fix it and try again.

check: When we find a bug we stay...
lessons.try: Share a time you fixed a mistake.

learn: Check one step at a time.
Does each step do what we want?
Find the first wrong step.
check: To find a bug, check ___ step at a time.
We look for the ___ wrong step.
lessons.try: Check a path step by step with your finger.

learn: Sometimes steps are in the wrong order.
Swap them to fix it.
Order matters.

To fix an order bug, ___ the steps.
lessons.try: Fix a mixed-up set of picture steps.

learn: Sometimes a step is missing.
The robot stops short.
Add the missing step.

learn: Try first, then ask a friend.

Helping each other is good teamwork.
lessons.try: Practise "Ask three before me".

learn: Bugs are mistakes.
Check step by step.
Fix and test again.
lessons.try: Fix three buggy robot paths.

learn: Always ask a grown-up before going online or using a new app.
If you see something scary or strange, tell a grown-up right away.
Grown-ups help keep you safe.
check: Before using a new app, you should...
If you see something scary, you...
lessons.try: With your family, make a rule list for using devices.

learn: Private information is about you that strangers should not know.
Your full name, address, school and passwords are private.
Do not share private information online.
check: Should you share your password with strangers?
lessons.try: Sort cards into okay to share and keep private.

learn: Screens are fun, but we also need to play outside, read and sleep.
Take breaks and rest your eyes.
A balanced day has many different activities.
lessons.try: Draw a balanced day with screen time, play, meals and sleep.

learn: Be kind online, just like in person.
Real people read what you send.
If words would hurt, don't send them.
lessons.try: Practise kind messages.

learn: If something online makes you feel bad, stop.
Tell a grown-up you trust.
You will not be in trouble for telling.
check: If something online feels wrong, first...
lessons.try: Name your trusted grown-ups.

learn: Some pop-ups say "Click here!"
Don't click things you don't know.
Ask a grown-up first.
check: A strange pop-up says "Click here!" You...
lessons.try: Sort safe and unsafe buttons on a pretend screen.

learn: When you are done, log off.
Logging off keeps your things private.
Don't share your login.

Ask: who made this?
Check with a grown-up.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Online Safety
learn: Ask before you click.
Keep private things private.
Be kind and tell a grown-up.

learn: A robot is a machine that can sense, think with a computer and move.
Some robots vacuum floors. Some build cars. Some explore Mars.
Robots follow programs that people write.
lessons.try: Draw a robot and tell what job it does.

learn: Robots use sensors to know about the world.
A camera lets a robot see. A bump sensor tells it when it hits something.
Sensors are like our eyes, ears and skin.
check: A bump sensor tells when it...
lessons.try: Play blindfolded robot: a partner guides you with gentle taps.

learn: Engineers design robots to solve problems.
First, think of a problem. Then draw a robot to help.
Share your idea and listen to others' ideas.

learn: Robot vacuums clean floors.
Robot lawn mowers cut grass.
They follow programs.

learn: Robots build cars in factories.
Robots help doctors.
Robots carry boxes in warehouses.

People send them instructions from Earth.

learn: Robots follow programs.
Robots sense and move.
Robots help people.

learn: In coding stories, a character does actions: walk, jump, say hello.

The scene is where the story happens.

check: Where the story happens is the...

A say block shows words.

check: A move block makes a character...

First, next, last.
